title: Count Caesar Cipher Pairs
summary: Given an array of n strings, each consisting of lowercase English letters and having the same length m, count the number of pairs of indices (i, j) where i < j and the strings at these indices are similar.
statement: Given an array of n strings, each consisting of lowercase English letters and having the same length m, count the number of pairs of indices (i, j) where i < j and the strings at these indices are similar. Two strings are considered similar if one can be transformed into the other by cyclically shifting each character to the next letter in the alphabet.
constraints: All words have the same length and total input size is at most 100,000.
One operation shifts every character of one chosen word forward cyclically by one.
Count index pairs whose words differ by one uniform cyclic shift.
hints: Uniform shifts preserve every character’s modular difference from the first character.
Normalize a word to the tuple (char-first) mod 26, whose first component is zero.
Count earlier identical keys while scanning words.
Two words have the same normalized differences exactly when one uniform cyclic shift transforms one into the other.
editorial: Two words have the same normalized differences exactly when one uniform cyclic shift transforms one into the other.
